claims.text: The dispute is rider-filed and the charge is still live: EV-FARE-00208 shows a total_charged of 8.00, a cancellation-fee line of 8.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, so on a rider filing it leaves the $8.00 where it is; FULL_REFUND and PARTIAL_REFUND return the contested amount to her; ESCALATE holds it rather than collecting it. What the rider is arguing for is therefore a ruling under which she stops carrying this charge, not the size of the driver's payout.

I do not press the rider's central assertion that the driver never came, because the record does not support it. EV-GPS-00208 puts the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for one continuous run of 585 seconds, from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55, and the 'arrived' event at 16:02:25 recorded on EV-TRIP-00208 falls inside that run; the arrival test in POL-NS-02 is satisfied and the dwell limb of POL-NS-01 is met with 285 seconds to spare against the 300 second free waiting period in force. POL-NS-06's shortfall route needs a dwell below 300 seconds, so it is closed on these numbers, and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0): no advisory covers this road, so no advisory-based accumulation or excuse is on the record for either party. I state this plainly rather than stretch the trace.

The rider's other exoneration route, POL-NS-04, cannot be run in her favour and I do not pretend otherwise. Her 16:08:02 message on EV-CHAT-00208 ('coming coming 2 min') is followed by the driver's reply at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds later, and by an in-app call placed by the driver at 16:09:40 that EV-TRIP-00208 records as answered, lasting 34 seconds; so limb (b) fails, because the driver both replied within 120 seconds and called before terminating. Limb (c) also fails affirmatively: EV-GPS-00208 places the rider's device 633 to 646 m from the pin, with rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider radius. POL-NS-11 is why the clause simply cannot help her. The log does show a rider who read each of the driver's messages within about half a minute — but responsiveness is not what limb (b) tests.

On the face of the clause that authorises this charge, the rider is entitled to the full refund: POL-NS-01 states that where the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the radius, 'the fee is not chargeable, the ruling is FULL_REFUND of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation'. The fixed points of this trip are exactly that case — EV-GPS-00208 counts 60 qualifying driver fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius, and EV-TRIP-00208 records no boarding event — and the rider asks the Judge to give those words effect. I accept two things against myself: the sentence sits in the clause's discussion of reason codes, and the driver used a recognised code (RIDER_NO_SHOW); and POL-NS-02's closing sentence reads the in-radius case as turning on dwell duration, which the Judge may hold. But the sentence's operative condition is the position of the driver's own fixes, the 'mis-selected reason code' it mentions is a consequential referral rather than a precondition, and a clause that takes money from a rider should not be resolved against her on a tension inside its own drafting.

If the Judge does not take the POL-NS-01 point, and cannot resolve the tension between POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-02's closing sentence on these facts, the rider's fallback is that the case goes to a person instead of being left where it is. POL-GEN-07 forbids the Judge to construct an outcome where the clauses in force do not license one, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected or refunded, so the 8.00 shown as CHARGED on EV-FARE-00208 would not sit with the rider while the question is open. A hold is the outcome the rider prefers to a NO_ACTION that quietly leaves the charge in place.

Two profile facts in this file are not available as grounds against the rider, and the Judge should say so in the reasoning. EV-RPROF-00208 records prior_no_show_flags 3, a lifetime counter, while no_show_disputes_30d is 1 — below the threshold of 3 that POL-NS-09(d) sets; that limb reads only the trailing-30-day field and states in terms that the lifetime counter is not the field it reads and may not be substituted for it, so no escalation and no adverse finding may rest on it. POL-GEN-01 makes prior_no_show_flags, the 4.66 rating, the 0.071 cancellation rate and the 4 prior disputes filed with 1 upheld context only: they may inform how closely her assertions are scrutinised, but they can never establish a fact about this trip or carry a finding against her.

The rider asked for a person in the words of her own filing — 'I want somebody to call me about this'. POL-GEN-08(3) gives either party the right, at any time before execution and once after, to have the dispute decided by a human, and that request is never refused on the ground that the automated ruling was correct. The rider asks that the request be recorded and honoured, and that the coordination history on EV-CHAT-00208 — her reply, the driver's two waiting messages and the answered call — be read by that person before the charge against her becomes final.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25, and the driver's own unbroken 10-second trace places him inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius before that event: his first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 16:02:10, 15 seconds ahead of the marker, and the trace yields 60 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius (far more than the three consecutive fixes the clause requires), with a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 28.8 m. Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on the strongest possible evidence — the driver's own GPS, not his assertion.

The driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous 585 seconds, from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55 — 285 seconds more than the 300-second free waiting period in force for this LARGE_VENUE trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and more than the 300-second minimum_dwell_sec for this zone class in the fee schedule. Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied and POL-NS-06's shortfall branch is unreachable: the computed shortfall is negative by 285 seconds, so this is a surplus, not a shortfall.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 — five minutes after the required dwell elapsed at 16:07:10 — with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) of POL-NS-01 expressly recognises, and the record shows no boarding event and no started trip. Limb (d) is satisfied, and the reason code is not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, so the branch of POL-NS-01 that addresses that code does not arise on this trip.

POL-NS-05 does not bite. The arrival marker is not false: at the 16:02:25 marker the driver was stationary within 28.8 m of the pickup pin — nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger or the 15 km/h motion trigger — and the trace records his in-geofence speed as 0.0 km/h throughout the 585-second run. Nothing here even approaches the false-arrival thresholds, so the waiting clock needs no recomputation and runs from the genuine arrival.

This is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case under POL-NS-03. That clause governs only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; here the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the radius, at a minimum of 28.8 m from the pin, so POL-NS-03 yields and the fee is decided under POL-NS-01.

The rider's own device contradicts her account of waiting at the guardhouse for fifteen minutes. Across 141 fixes from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20 the rider's track never moves (a single distinct speed, 0.0 km/h) and sits 633.9 m to 646.4 m from the pickup pin — zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for this zone class. On her own telemetry she was not at the pickup point at any moment while the driver waited there.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on any limb. Limb (b) fails outright: the driver replied in the chat at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds after the rider's 16:08:02 'coming coming 2 min', and he placed an in-app voice call at 16:09:40 which the trip record shows was answered and lasted 34 seconds — so the driver neither stayed silent for 120 seconds nor failed to call. Limb (c) fails on the rider's own track, as set out above.

No traffic advisory covers Depot Road in this window: EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-NS-06(i) aggregation across multiple in-geofence intervals is unavailable and I do not rely on it. The driver does not need it: his single in-geofence interval of 585 seconds already clears the 300-second minimum on its own, and POL-NS-06(ii) confirms an advisory can never reduce the required minimum anyway.

Nothing in this bundle is impaired for policy purposes and no POL-NS-08 limb fires: the trace has 100% coverage, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and the expected 10-second sampling across the whole waiting window; the chat log holds all six messages that trip_record.chat_message_count records, with no numbering gap; and the SGD 8.00 cancellation-fee line equals the platform_policy figure for this RYDE_XL trip, so limb (d) is not engaged. The arrival-event timestamp and the GPS fix timestamps are 15 seconds apart, far inside the 90-second skew threshold.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 8.00 fee in force — SGD 6.40 — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip and cannot trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause requires, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, far below the 0.08 rate threshold. Both limbs are required and neither is met.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires and this case is decidable without a human reviewer. The artifacts are admissible and agree with one another; the two parties show 0 disputes with each other in the trailing 90 days; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not tripped; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires. There is no direct contradiction on arrival, dwell or rider presence for limb (b) to catch, and no artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) for limb (e) to catch.

The charge stands as it presently stands. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and because this dispute was filed by the rider, leaving the charge in place is precisely the disposition the evidence supports: the rider's claim is not supported, the SGD 8.00 fee is not refunded, and the driver is paid SGD 6.40 under POL-NS-07. The driver performed every element of the no-show contract — he arrived at the pin, held it for 585 seconds, messaged twice with his plate, replied within 18 seconds, and placed an answered 34-second call — and the fee is the consideration he earned.

ruling.explanation:
This was a verified no-show: the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee stands and the driver is paid SGD 6.40.

What the record shows. The driver's 10-second GPS trace (EV-GPS-00208) puts his vehicle inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius at The Interlace guardhouse from 16:02:10, and he held position there continuously for 585 seconds until 16:11:55 — 285 seconds more than the 300-second free waiting period in force for this RYDE_XL trip under the trip record's platform policy (EV-TRIP-00208). The 'arrived' marker at 16:02:25 sits inside that run with only 15 seconds of skew, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises — with no boarding event. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them.

Rider, on your account. Your statement that the driver never came is not borne out, and your advocate rightly did not press it. Your own device track (EV-GPS-00208) never moves and stays 634–646 m from the pickup pin, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius — you were not at the guardhouse pickup point while the driver waited. POL-NS-04 therefore does not exonerate you: limb (b) fails because the driver replied 18 seconds after your 16:08:02 message and placed an answered 34-second in-app call at 16:09:40 (EV-CHAT-00208, EV-TRIP-00208), and limb (c) fails on your own fixes. POL-NS-06 cannot help you, because the dwell exceeded the free waiting period, and no traffic advisory exists to change that (EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Your reading of POL-NS-01's 'fixes inside the radius' sentence is rejected: read with the clause's own note, that sentence is the in-radius DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE outcome only, and the driver here used RIDER_NO_SHOW. The arrival marker was not false — the driver was stationary 28.8 m from the pin at 0 km/h — so POL-NS-05 does not fire and the waiting clock runs from the genuine arrival. Because the clauses do license an outcome, there is no gap for POL-GEN-07 to fill and no basis for escalation.

Driver compensation and the profiles. Because the fee is chargeable and nothing displaces it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80% of the SGD 8.00 fee — SGD 6.40 — the residual 20% retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2/143 = 0.014 (below 0.08), and both limbs must be met. Under POL-GEN-03 a ruling that pays the driver is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd carries the same figure, SGD 6.40. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: the admissible artifacts agree with one another, there is no shared-party dispute history, the anti-farming check is not tripped, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3). Your prior_no_show_flags of 3, your rating, cancellation rate and prior dispute counters are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not used as a ground against you.

Integrity and confidence. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d): the trace has 100% coverage and a 0.0 s maximum gap, the chat log carries the 6 messages the trip record counts, the SGD 8.00 fare line reconciles to the platform figure, and the clock skew is 15 seconds. The deciding facts rest on artifacts of full weight (1.0), so confidence is set at 0.95.

Referrals and next steps. No clause produces a referral here: the arrival marker was not false (POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire) and the POL-NS-07 check did not trip. Your request for someone to call you is noted in this ruling; it does not itself create a referral, but you retain the right to ask for a human decision (POL-GEN-08(3)) and the appeal route under POL-GEN-04. The monetary effect, SGD 6.40, is within the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue.

ledger.claim: The rider asked for a person in the words of her own filing — 'I want somebody to call me about this'. POL-GEN-08(3) gives either party the right, at any time before execution and once after, to have the dispute decided by a human, and that request is never refused on the ground that the automated ruling was correct. The rider asks that the request be recorded and honoured, and that the coordination history on EV-CHAT-00208 — her reply, the driver's two waiting messages and the answered call — be read by that person before the charge against her becomes final.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25, and the driver's own unbroken 10-second trace places him inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius before that event: his first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 16:02:10, 15 seconds ahead of the marker, and the trace yields 60 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius (far more than the three consecutive fixes the clause requires), with a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 28.8 m. Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on the strongest possible evidence — the driver's own GPS, not his assertion.

The driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous 585 seconds, from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55 — 285 seconds more than the 300-second free waiting period in force for this LARGE_VENUE trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and more than the 300-second minimum_dwell_sec for this zone class in the fee schedule. Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied and POL-NS-06's shortfall branch is unreachable: the computed shortfall is negative by 285 seconds, so this is a surplus, not a shortfall.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 — five minutes after the required dwell elapsed at 16:07:10 — with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) of POL-NS-01 expressly recognises, and the record shows no boarding event and no started trip. Limb (d) is satisfied, and the reason code is not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, so the branch of POL-NS-01 that addresses that code does not arise on this trip.

POL-NS-05 does not bite. The arrival marker is not false: at the 16:02:25 marker the driver was stationary within 28.8 m of the pickup pin — nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger or the 15 km/h motion trigger — and the trace records his in-geofence speed as 0.0 km/h throughout the 585-second run. Nothing here even approaches the false-arrival thresholds, so the waiting clock needs no recomputation and runs from the genuine arrival.

This is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case under POL-NS-03. That clause governs only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; here the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the radius, at a minimum of 28.8 m from the pin, so POL-NS-03 yields and the fee is decided under POL-NS-01.

The rider's own device contradicts her account of waiting at the guardhouse for fifteen minutes. Across 141 fixes from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20 the rider's track never moves (a single distinct speed, 0.0 km/h) and sits 633.9 m to 646.4 m from the pickup pin — zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for this zone class. On her own telemetry she was not at the pickup point at any moment while the driver waited there.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on any limb. Limb (b) fails outright: the driver replied in the chat at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds after the rider's 16:08:02 'coming coming 2 min', and he placed an in-app voice call at 16:09:40 which the trip record shows was answered and lasted 34 seconds — so the driver neither stayed silent for 120 seconds nor failed to call. Limb (c) fails on the rider's own track, as set out above.

No traffic advisory covers Depot Road in this window: EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-NS-06(i) aggregation across multiple in-geofence intervals is unavailable and I do not rely on it. The driver does not need it: his single in-geofence interval of 585 seconds already clears the 300-second minimum on its own, and POL-NS-06(ii) confirms an advisory can never reduce the required minimum anyway.

Nothing in this bundle is impaired for policy purposes and no POL-NS-08 limb fires: the trace has 100% coverage, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and the expected 10-second sampling across the whole waiting window; the chat log holds all six messages that trip_record.chat_message_count records, with no numbering gap; and the SGD 8.00 cancellation-fee line equals the platform_policy figure for this RYDE_XL trip, so limb (d) is not engaged.
